hold_text: ⚠️ THIS WAS DISPATCHED AS 'Tier-1, land it yourself once green' AND THE REPO'S OWN GUARD REFUSES THAT. pr-landing-guard R5: `config/lever_reachability.json` is Tier-2 by path, so self-landing is refused on it -- 'a path outside TIER1_SURFACE is not thereby dangerous; it is one the guard cannot certify'. I did not override it. Splitting further does not help either: the guard registered here FAILS when an entry carries a reach-share verdict with no `evidence` block, so the script and the registry blocks have to land in one change or CI goes red. So this needs one human OK, and it is a small one -- the change writes no value that anything branches on.
why: CI tooling plus a measurement record. Adds scripts/ops/lever_evidence_flag.py (read-only over config/lever_reachability.json), registers it as `lever-evidence-flag-guard` in scripts/ci/run_guards.py, and writes an `evidence` block (k, n, interval, flag) onto each registry entry plus the `evidence_flag_policy` block the script reads its policy from. NO strategy parameter, no runtime code, no order path, no account or roster change -- config/lever_reachability.json 'RECORDS MEASUREMENTS AND DISPOSITIONS; it changes no behaviour and no value' by its own header.
note: Deliberately split from the Tier-3 arm-strip PR #12737, which also stays `landing: hold`. This is meant to land FIRST so the strip PR can cite the flag: a strip proposed on 0/8 is a proposal to delete a lever we cannot show is dead, and the operator must see it in those terms. The two cut-points in evidence_flag_policy are PROPOSED and are an operator decision; the block says so and nothing outside this script branches on them.
